subject: Compare sliders must remain true full-range sliders on desktop and mobile
root_cause: Legacy/custom gesture handling and edge clamping could prevent the visual handle from reaching the physical 0% and 100% endpoints, especially on iOS/touch, leaving one side's content unreadable.
permanent_invariants: Every compare slider uses one canonical 0-100 state model.
Desktop and mobile remain true reveal sliders; mobile must never be replaced by stacked cards as a workaround.
The active gesture surface must allow physical access to both endpoints, not merely report 0 or 100 internally.
A native full-width range control provides the fail-safe touch/keyboard path and must span the complete slider width without edge clamp.
ARIA min/max/current values must stay synchronized with the canonical slider state.
Legacy listeners may not regain ownership or re-clamp the endpoints after canonical initialization.
Late page/build CSS may not introduce a separate slider variable or endpoint clamp.
A release is not complete until real browser/touch validation proves left and right physical endpoints and production readback is green.
verified_evidence: PR #1173 merged the native full-range iOS/touch fix.
Protected test checks passed on the release head.
Production readback on the merge SHA completed successfully.
A later main production readback also passed, proving the fix survived subsequent repository drift.
prevention_rule: Never accept a slider fix based only on CSS appearance or numeric state. Require canonical state ownership, physical 0/100 endpoint reachability on real browser/touch automation, readable content at both extremes, and exact production readback before declaring the issue closed.
